newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses fall on Dow drop, dlr pressured.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses fall on Dow drop, dlr pressured.

text.p: Equity markets in London, Frankfurt and Paris fell on Wednesday morning, hit by a large overnight decline on Wall Street.

In currency markets, the dollar came under fresh pressure after a hawkish assessment on German inflation from the Bundesbank was seen as raising the chances of German interest rate rises and boosted the mark across the board.
London traders took a fairly relaxed view of the Wall Street's decline, which saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average lose 101.27 points to 7960.84.
Initially, the FTSE-100 index of leading shares was some 25 points lower after finishing at its second highest ever level on Tuesday at 5075.8.
"The (London) market is not immune but it is used to these big swings on Wall St," said Charterhouse group economist Richard Jeffrey.

Dealers were less sanguine, however, about the latest British unemployment data, published an hour after the market opened. July figures showed an unexpectedly low jobless rate of 5.5 percent, down from 5.7 percent in June.
This was a larger fall than the market had bargained for and by 1030 GMT the FTSE-100 decline had moved up a gear, showing a loss of 48.3 points, a 0.95 percent fall, to 5027.5.
The Bank of England's August inflation report, released later, signalled that monetary policy may stay on hold after four successive monthly rate rises.

"The Monetary Policy Committee concluded that monetary policy has now reached a position at which it should be possible to pause in order to assess the direction in which the risks (to inflation) are likly to materialise," the central bank said.
The pound took little notice of the report, but was up from earlier lows against the mark and dollar at 2.9290/00 marks and $1.5820/30.

In Frankfurt, the situation was similar. The DAX index lost 1.4 percent in early trade to 4,303.78. Dealers there said sentiment was undermined by the failure of the Dow Jones to close above the psychologically important 8,000 point level.

Monday's Wall Street drop was not the only negative U.S. influence on European stocks. Nervousness about U.S. July producer price and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT was also making dealers edgy about any possible inflationary signs.

French dealers were particularly anxious about the upcoming U.S. numbers, which are expected to show a 0.1 percent rise in the producer price index and and 0.7 percent rise in retail sales. The CAC-40 index was 50.1 points lower at 2,948.47 by 0923 GMT.
The dollar slid to early lows at 1.8500/10 after a warning on inflation from Germany's Bundesbank boosted the mark.

In its August monthly report, published early on Wednesday, the Bundesbank said it could not overlook a stronger rise in consumer prices in the last few months, and would orientate its policy in such a way that price stability can be maintained.

"The assertion that the exchange rate is very significant in policy decisions, the fact that they highlight the recent rise in some inflation figures and the desire to see M3 growth lower, suggest they may be closer to a rate increase than previously thought," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
On Tuesday, data for July showed that German inflation rose to 1.9 percent, the highest level since June 1995 and up from 1.7 percent in June.

Even though the CPI data was boosted by one-off factors last month, economists expect it to rise above 2.0 percent soon, the level regarded as acceptable by the Bundesbank. German import prices, due to be released later this month, are also key for signs whether the weakness of the mark is boosting inflation.
A report from the Bank of England
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.8513/19 marks and 116.39 yen, compared with 1.8665 and 115.78 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 48.0 points at 5,027.8.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 54.91 points at 4308.18.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 64.57 at 2934.00.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was $2.45 an ounce firmer in London at $328.60. Silver was up four cents at $4.47.
